title: How Lawson helped Lindblad by sacrificing his Q3 run
excerpt:
Grid penalties can often lead to different strategies in Formula 1 Qualifying. Typically if they are destined to start at the back the drivers concerned only make a token effort in Q1, and either don’t appear later in the session, or perhaps switch to helping their team mate with a tow – as was the case with Gabriel Bortoleto and his Audi partner Nico Hulkenberg in Austin.

Teams also always have to avoid tricky situations where, for example, a penalised driver bumps his unpenalised team mate down the order so that he doesn’t progress to the next session.

Saturday’s United States Grand Prix Qualifying saw an unusual take on the theme. A driver who had made the top 10 in Q2 and didn’t have a grid penalty was kept in the garage during Q3 in order to help his team mate – who did have a penalty.

This was the story that unfolded at Racing Bulls after Arvid Lindblad came into the weekend with a five-place drop for taking a new ICE.

The VCARB 03 had enough pace to head the midfield pack, and thus Lindblad and his team mate Liam Lawson were both able to make it to Q3.

Given that the cars ahead of them were the eight from the four top teams, and there were no Audis or Alpines in the mix, they were always destined to finish the final session in P9 and P10.

And in order to ensure that Lindblad got the higher position, which would convert to P14 on the final grid, the decision was made to not allow Lawson to run in Q3 – something that naturally went against his racer’s instincts.

He was thus classified P10 with no time achieved, but he will start a place ahead after Lindblad drops down the order.

"I would have loved to have a go at Q3,” said the New Zealander. “We actually got there with two sets as well, which is not normal for us. In a normal situation, if we're fighting an Alpine or an Audi, having those two sets would have been great to use.

“I would have loved to have a go at it, but considering Arvid's got a penalty, we were going to be ninth and 10th anyway, it just doesn't really make sense. Now we have plenty of tyres for tomorrow.”

Lindblad, Colapinto and Bortoleto penalised for US GP

Lawson admitted that it wasn’t easy to climb out of the cockpit and watch his team mate head out of the garage. “I asked to go out, to be honest," he added. "I said I want to go and do it, and they said no. So yeah, it's frustrating a little bit for a driver, especially because we've had a very strong weekend so far.

“The car's been very good. Q1 on one set, we were comfortably through. Q2 was a little bit more tricky to be honest. But going to Q3 with two sets of tyres would have would have been lots of fun.”

Crucially, given the battle for P5 in the Constructors' Championship, Lawson starts immediately ahead of Alpine’s Pierre Gasly.

“To be fair, it was very, very close with Pierre in Q2,” he said. “But obviously we're one set less at that point. We were ready to go if we needed to in Q3 there. The car's been good in the long run as well. So hopefully tomorrow we can have a good race.”

Lindblad meanwhile was pleased with how the session turned out, although he too was compromised in that he only did one run in Q3 when he had the tyres available for a second.

“I think it makes sense what we did,” he said. “For sure, I would have loved to have another go. We both had an extra set left, and we were close I think to P8 in Q2, but realistically, the top teams always pull another gear when we get to Q3.

“So realistically, we would have both been in the same position we are now – maybe gone half a second or six-tenths quicker. But I was happy with Q2.”

Heading the midfield pack is always an achievement, so was there some frustration at not being able to start from the P9 he originally earned?

“Yeah, I guess so,” he said. “But at the same time I knew coming into the weekend I would take the penalty. I mean, it's a bit of a shame that it was only two races ago I was taking a penalty already, but it is what it is. That's just the nature of how things are with the new engines this year.

“But very happy with today. It's not been an easy week. I've been slower than Liam in every session so far – I think eight or nine-tenths slower than him in the first run of Q1. So to be ahead at the end of Q2 when it mattered, I'm obviously very happy with.

“But at the same time, looking ahead to tomorrow now because that's where the points are scored, I think on this track, overtaking is possible. So just being with a good pace will help us to come through.”

title: ‘We can’t fix core problems' – Albon on Williams' Qualifying
excerpt:
Alex Albon conceded Williams were struggling to "fix core problems" as the team's struggles at the United States Grand Prix weekend continued with another disappointing day.

After finishing bottom of the timesheets in both FP1 and FP2, the Thai driver made some improvement in FP3 by finishing ahead of team mate Carlos Sainz and the Cadillac pairing of Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas, but remained almost 2.8 seconds off the pace of Lewis Hamilton at the front.

Things did not get any better for Williams though in Saturday's Qualifying session, with both drivers eliminated in Q1 after struggling to keep the car on track at the Circuit of The Americas.

Sainz, who admitted on Friday that he “wasn’t expecting any miracles” across this United States Grand Prix weekend, will start in P17 on Sunday, while Albon will line-up one place behind him in P18 as the pair were elevated two spots thanks to the grid penalties for Franco Colapinto and Gabriel Bortoleto.

When asked for his instant reaction to Saturday’s Qualifying runs, a confused Albon admitted: “Maybe we need to review our run plan a bit. I felt like we went out really early on the last run.

“We’ve been fighting a lot with the car, with the tyres. Honestly, I finished Qualifying just as confused as I was in FP1. We were trying everything. We’re doing different set-ups every session and yet we can’t fix core problems in the car.

“We throw stuff at the wall – spaghetti at the wall, I guess – and hope that it sticks, but nothing sticks. Let’s see tomorrow.”

The frustration is clear inside the Williams garage, although the disappointing results in Austin have been partly blamed on the ongoing tests taking place as they look further ahead towards the 2027 season.

Speaking after Qualifying, Sainz explained: “It’s been a general weekend where we’ve invested a lot into next year and probably didn’t maximise the car until the last laps of Qualifying. I did some really good laps and we changed a few things on the set-up that helped me be a bit more comfortable today, especially in that Qualifying session.

“On that last lap I was probably just pushing too hard. I did a mega Sector 1, mega Sector 2 and unfortunately I couldn’t close the lap. Maybe with a perfect Sector 3 we could’ve put it in towards the top end of Q1 or even Q2, but I’ll take it.

“I think we’ve been brave with the set-up and testing a few things. I was quite brave on that lap, but unfortunately I did a mistake towards the end and I couldn’t close it.

"We’re definitely learning a few things about next year. We are investing a lot in it, but it’s also true that we cannot hide the fact that we have a very poor car at a track like Austin.

“Not even with investing all that time developing all those things for next year, we would be any better today. We are slow – it’s what it is. We’re trying our best, but until the end of the year I don’t expect any miracles.”

title: Palmowski crowned 2026 champion as Larsen takes maiden victory
excerpt:
Alisha Palmowski has secured the 2026 F1 ACADEMY Drivers’ title after recovering from eighth to second in the Reverse Grid Race in Austin, as Ferrari’s Alba Larsen claimed her maiden victory in the series.

The Red Bull Racing driver entered the race with a 63-point advantage over closest rival Emma Felbermayr, starting immediately ahead of the Audi driver in eighth. However, a strong recovery through the field was enough to seal the title with three races remaining.

Reverse Grid polesitter Rafaela Ferreira retained the lead at the start, but contact involving the Racing Bulls driver and Jade Jacquet brought out an early Safety Car, with Wild Card Alexia Danielsson hitting the stricken Williams car.

Larsen capitalised on the incident to take the lead and the Ferrari driver controlled the race from the restart, while Gatorade’s Lisa Billard moved into second after overtaking the damaged car of Ferreira around the outside of Turn 1.

Behind them, Palmowski and Felbermayr battled their way through the field, with the Briton gaining the upper hand as both drivers passed Nina Gademan. A penalty for third-place Natalia Granada for a starting procedure infringement subsequently promoted Palmowski into P3, before she overtook Billard for second to put herself in position to secure the title.

Larsen maintained her advantage to take her first F1 ACADEMY victory by 2.3s, having finished on the podium in each of her previous three races. Palmowski crossed the line in second to become the series’ fourth champion, while Billard completed the podium by securing her maiden top-three finish.

Felbermayr finished fourth ahead of Gademan in fifth, with Mercedes’ Payton Westcott taking sixth. Megan Bruce finished seventh, while Ella Lloyd claimed the final point in eighth.

With the drivers’ title decided, attention turns to Sunday’s Feature Race at 1200 local time, with champion Palmowski lining up on pole and hunting down her sixth win of 2026.

title: What are the tyre strategy options for the United States GP?
excerpt:
You really do have to wonder who writes Kimi Antonelli’s scripts. The Mercedes driver has the hand of history on his shoulder, poised to become the youngest F1 World Champion, and with potential to seal the deal here in Austin.

It’ll require a victory and everything else going his way, but he gave himself the best possible chance of that by popping-up in Q3 with a scintillating pole position lap, after the timesheets in Q1 and Q2 had been topped by World Champions Lando Norris and Max Verstappen respectively.

And while it’s the Dutchman who looks like being the most serious competition for the victory, the top four teams, while individually strong in different sectors, are separated by a spread of only 0.12s on long-run pace. COTA offers decent overtaking opportunities, and plenty of scope for strategy to play its part. So let’s dive in…

title: Hamilton explains Ferrari’s Qualifying deficit in Austin
excerpt:
Not for the first time in 2026, Ferrari’s strong practice pace did not translate into Qualifying, with the Scuderia losing out in Austin to Mercedes and Red Bull in the battle at the front.

After setting the pace on Friday, Charles Leclerc had to settle for fourth in Q3, while FP3 pace-setter Lewis Hamilton could do no better than fifth, just 0.044s behind his team mate.

Hamilton was happy with the behaviour of his car and pointed to Ferrari’s straight-line performance as one reason for their drop-off relative to their rivals.

“We know through the weekend we look at the straight, like just up to Turn 1, when we cut power, they just keep pulling,” he said. “That's similar in other places, like going into Turn 11.

“I think we might be similar in maybe into 12, but then the rest of the lap, a little bit. You see it on the overlay. I don't know what happened. My car felt really good. Lap was solid, so they were just quicker.”

Hamilton believes that Ferrari's rivals have also improved their chassis of late, with the SF-26 having been acknowledged as the benchmark for much of the season.

“Car felt good as I said, so it was a clean lap, no issues at all, really,” he noted. “So, I think that's the only place we lose [the straight]. I think our car is really solid. I mean, at least as good, if not maybe slightly better, maybe than the others.

“But I think they have closed up on chassis. You've seen the Red Bull closed up on their downforce. Mercedes took a three-tenth step of upgrade at least a couple of races ago. I think they're starting to figure out how to utilise that, and so they're now matching us through the corners.

“And we're not able to take that step, in this season, to close that speed on the straight.”

Pressed on how good the Red Bull Ford power unit is at the moment Hamilton said: “It varies. I mean, I haven't seen the actual numbers this weekend. I think this morning it was like three-tenths, but in some places three to five tenths, maybe it's four-tenths. It's pretty impressive.

“I don't know if you see the overlays, but into Turn 1, ours starts dipping, and theirs just keeps going. So that's hard to compete with.

“If we had the same power as them, we would be right there in the battle. I think we'd probably be on the front row. But we know that that's the case, so we try to make the best we can out of it.”

While Hamilton was happy with how his car performed in Qualifying, Leclerc was not. He conceded that he didn’t have an optimum out lap, and thus his tyres were not quite in the window.

“It's very disappointing,” said the Monegasque driver. “Because I think there are some other weekends where we've been strong in free practices, but then coming quali, it's very clear that the others are just having a lot more in the straights, and it's very difficult for us to match that.

“But I felt like today it's a Qualifying where we had the potential in the car. But the car also includes tyres. And in Q3, unfortunately, we were not in the right place, and it was like one or two degrees less in Q3, and for me it was a huge difference.

“Just really struggled in the out lap – I was sliding quite a lot already from the out lap, and that made it very difficult after that.”

Leclerc said Ferrari now need to understand why extracting performance in Q3 is proving more difficult.

“It is quite frustrating, but there are reasons for it,” he said. “And so at the same time, I think we just need to work harder and try and understand very well those tyres, even better than what we are doing now, because the others, I think, normally have a bit more.

“It's a bit easier for them to extract the lap time in Q3 than it is for us. And as soon as we are a tiny bit outside the window, we pay a lot the price. So this is something that we need to look into.”

Despite Ferrari’s Qualifying deficit, Hamilton remains hopeful of making progress in Sunday’s race.

“You have to be realistic,” said Hamilton. “We're fourth and fifth. It's very hard to overtake here. Even if you're P2 on the grid, it's hard to beat someone on race distance.

“In 2012 it took a lot to get past Vettel back then. But maybe with strategy, we can progress. We can get a good run up into Turn 1 there's opportunities there for strategy, so we should see.”

title: What the teams said – Qualifying in the United States
excerpt:
The drivers and teams report back on all the action from final practice and Qualifying at the Circuit of The Americas ahead of the United States Grand Prix.

Oct 25, 2026 12:50am UTC

Mercedes

Kimi Antonelli certainly seemed in the mix on Saturday in COTA, but not many expected the Italian to grab pole by nearly two tenths of a second – including his own boss, Toto Wolff admitting afterwards that he thought P3 to P5 was likely. But Antonelli had other ideas, going out early and nailing his first lap in Q3. No one really improved on the second runs thanks to tricky wind conditions, meaning the youngster had grabbed his first pole since Spa and put himself in a great position to challenge for the win.

George Russell could not get close to his team mate, two scrappy runs in Q3 meaning he lines up only sixth. Both Mercedes cars made it through Q1 on the mediums though, so they do have a new set of softs to play with tomorrow.

Kimi Antonelli, 1st, 1:34.035

"I am really happy to take pole position as that was not an easy session. We progressed throughout qualifying, as we have done all weekend, but the ultimate lap time was not easy to come by. We have focused on building up to the limit, getting the car in a good place and then trusting that we can extract the performance when it matters. We have been working really hard with this update to get it into a good window so that is perhaps the most satisfying thing to take from today. I was surprised to take P1; it felt like a good lap though and it's a great result for the team because they've done a tremendous job on this package and we are now seeing results.

"My focus for tomorrow is purely on driving the best race I can. I hope that we can fight for the win, but we will know it won't be easy. Our closest competitors have looked very quick, but we will aim to get a good start then take it from there."

George Russell, 6th, 1:34.476

"We have made some good improvements with the car this weekend and moved it into a good window. The updates have proved really positive and my qualifying session was going well until we got to Q3. Ultimately it was just two bad laps from my side and that is why we ended up P6. Kimi did a great job to take pole and that shows what the car was capable of.

"Tomorrow will be a long race where strategy will play a big role. There are usually incidents here that change how the Grand Prix is playing out so we will be looking for opportunities to move forward. Our pace on Friday was relatively strong so that is encouraging. We will be giving it our all to score some good points."

Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport

"Taking pole position today was beyond our expectations heading into the session. We've been working hard to get the car into a good window all weekend, and we've been chipping away at it. Ahead of qualifying though I thought we were probably fighting to sneak onto the front row but more likely for P3 or P4. Kimi pulled out an incredible lap in Q3 to take pole position to surprise us all. George wasn't happy with his efforts in the final segment of qualifying, but he still did a solid job in what was a highly competitive session.

"What is clear with our updates is that the car now has a narrower window of operation. If we manage to get everything together then the performance is strong. We are still learning but this is another encouraging sign that we are still moving in the right direction. Tomorrow's race will be a big test, and we know our competitors are strong, but we can hopefully fight for victory and bring home a good points score as a team."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"Congratulations to Kimi and the team on a well-deserved pole position. Since introducing our latest updates, we've found it difficult to get the car into a consistent balance window. Our experience this weekend suggests that remains the case, but we've at least shown that the performance is there when we can get everything into the sweet spot.

"We made some reasonably large changes overnight based on the simulator work, and both drivers felt the car was a step in the right direction today. We were still struggling through the final sector though, with almost all our deficit to our competitors coming through the sequence from Turns 12 to 15.

"Kimi managed that section very well on his first run in Q3 and put together an impressive lap to take pole. George couldn't match his Q2 time though. His final lap started with a very strong first sector, but a small mistake at Turn 11 pushed the tyre temperatures up and he didn't have the grip from there to recover. Kimi had a similar drop-off on his final attempt, but fortunately his first lap was good enough to secure P1.

"Tomorrow will be a tough race. Some of our competitors have saved new Soft tyres and, from what we saw on Friday, the top four teams look very closely matched on race pace. Kimi is in the best possible position to fight for the win, whilst with George we should have some strategic options to help him move forward."

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Pole position qualifier Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy and Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team looks on during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

Red Bull

Max Verstappen has been in the mix here from word go, and despite a few complaints from the Dutchman in FP3, he always looked set to fight for pole. That is exactly what transpired, but Verstappen ran wide on his final lap and had to settle for P2. Isack Hadjar had a much more topsy turvy day, struggling hugely in FP3 and being called to the stewards to explain a moment where he appeared to push Alex Albon off the track.

But come Qualifying, the late changes he made to his car paid dividends and he pushed his team mate all the way through. In the end he grabbed third place, just 0.036s behind the Dutchman. Like Mercedes, Red Bull managed to save some soft tyres throughout Qualifying to give themselves strategy options for the race.

Max Verstappen, 2nd, 1:34.214

“P2 is a good starting position for tomorrow and overall we’ve been competitive throughout Qualifying. It’s been very close between a lot of cars all weekend and we were looking strong in Q2, but unfortunately in Q3 we couldn’t quite get the balance together. We didn’t have the same level of grip and I struggled to keep the rear of the car under control. The wind also picked up, which made the final sector particularly tricky, and there were a few corners that just didn’t come together, which was a shame. It’s been difficult to manage the tyres and understand when to push and when not to - that will be important tomorrow. Hopefully we can find the right balance between the low and high-speed corners, have good pace in clean air and be in the fight up front. I enjoy this track and we want to win, so that’s what we’ll go for. Congratulations to Alisha on her F1 Academy Championship, she’s been really strong all season so it’s great to see her bring it home today."

Isack Hadjar, 3rd, 1:34.250

“Third is a really great result from Qualifying. We’ve struggled this weekend to find the car I knew we had. Yesterday, and even this morning, things didn’t go our way. We just hadn’t been able to get things to click. To go from that to P3 is a great feeling. I’m really happy with how the Team continued pushing to find the right set-up; we didn’t sit around waiting for things to come to us. The car came alive right from the start of Q1, and I knew we were in a good place. Honestly, I felt Pole was there for the taking, and to be disappointed not to have it is a good sign of where we’re at. Max and I are up at the front, so we’ll try and use that to our advantage tomorrow. We’re in the fight, that’s for sure. A big congratulations to Alisha on winning the F1 Academy title, she's been super strong all year and I hope she enjoys the celebrations."

Laurent Mekies, Team Principal

"A really solid Qualifying from the whole Team, with both Max and Isack in the fight for Pole right up until the final run. Max had really strong laps in Q1 and Q2, but balance just slipped away in the final session, when the wind seemed to pick up and improvements were difficult to find for many drivers on their final laps.

"It was a trickier weekend for Isack up until Qualifying, as he had a few adjustments to make yesterday and again this morning. But with his engineers at the track and support from Milton Keynes, he kept chipping away. In Qualifying, he unlocked strong pace, and P3 matches his best Qualifying performance of the season.

"It will be a challenging race, and I think there are plenty of drivers with a chance of victory, but having Max on the front row and Isack right behind gives us a really good opportunity to be in the right battle tomorrow.

"Congratulations to Alisha on winning the F1 Academy Championship. This is a fantastic achievement and one she thoroughly deserves after an outstanding season.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands in the (3) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Pole position qualifier Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy and Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team and Third placed qualifier Isack Hadjar of France and Oracle Red Bull Racing celebrate in parc ferme during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Mark Thompson/Getty Images)

Ferrari

Lewis Hamilton topped FP3, meaning Ferrari had swept all three practice sessions. As such, they went into Qualifying as favourites for pole. But once again when it mattered their pace slightly disappeared, with Charles Leclerc managing fourth and Hamilton fifth. There was not much in it from second to sixth on the grid, but neither Scuderia driver could get near to Antonelli’s time.

Nevertheless, as Leclerc pointed out afterwards, the last time he won here, he did so from fourth on the grid. So if their race pace is strong, neither Ferrari car can be discounted from fighting forward tomorrow.

Lewis Hamilton, 5th, 1:34.311

"A big thank you to everyone back at the factory for the work they continue to do. The guys in the garage also did a great job today, and overall we’re in a good place.

"The car felt really good going into qualifying, and Q1 and Q2 were strong. Q3 felt pretty decent as well, but ultimately we weren’t quite close enough, so we’ll look into that and see where we can improve. Tomorrow won’t be easy, but we can still apply some pressure and with a good strategy and strong execution, hopefully put ourselves in a position to fight for the podium."

Charles Leclerc, 4th, 1 :34.267

"The start will be important tomorrow and from fourth we have the chance to work our way forward and fight for a podium, so that’s what we will focus on tonight. Qualifying was tricky in terms of getting the tyres up to temperature, especially in Q3 when the track cooled down, so we will look into that and understand how we can do better if this change in conditions happens again.

"The car feels good and we should be quite strong in the race, we will work together to bring home a good result for the whole team back home and our tifosi."

Fred Vasseur, Team Principal

"We have mixed feelings after this session, because for sure the potential was there and we showed good pace right from the start of the weekend. Up until the final corner of Q3 we were in the fight for pole, but that’s all part of the game. I think Q2 was a bit faster for everybody. We all struggled to improve in Q3, with the track conditions becoming a little more difficult, but it was the same for everyone.

"The front of the field is so close today that, by a couple of hundredths, you can move from P2 to P6, which can be just the difference of one metre at a braking point. Now we will focus on the race, because I think tomorrow could be a different story, and for sure it will be challenging with the high tyre degradation."

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Charles Leclerc of Monaco driving the (16) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Lewis Hamilton of Great Britain driving the (44) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images)

McLaren

It was not to be for McLaren, who looked fast in parts but also seemed to have a car that was difficult to handle. Neither Lando Norris nor Oscar Piastri could get the best out of the MCL40 on Saturday, with the World Champion not helped by losing his fastest lap time in Q3 to track limits. So, it didn't work out for them, but they are at least in the top 10 and can try and fight from there, especially if their car proves easier to handle in race trim.

Lando Norris, 8th, 1:35.049

“It was a disappointing end to the Qualifying session this afternoon. The car had the pace to be further up the order, but I didn’t put the lap together. It was challenging to drive today, especially in the corners with the wind making consistency across a complete lap difficult to achieve.

“Starting eighth makes tomorrow difficult, but the race is a long one, and the aim is to recover and make the most of the pace we have by taking the fight to the field. We’ll work hard as a team overnight to see where we can make gains to aim for a strong finish to the weekend.”

Oscar Piastri, 7th, 1:34.803

“That’s P7. We obviously wanted more from today. Overall, it has been a difficult weekend. The car has the potential to be quick, it’s just been hard to drive and we haven’t had the pace. Over the practice sessions and into Qualifying we tried a few different things, but while we weren’t expecting them to be a magic fix, they just haven’t quite done what we’ve wanted them to.

“We’ll keep working because there’s speed in the package—we just haven’t unlocked it yet. The focus now is on understanding how we can push the car further and extract the most out of tomorrow. If we can get ahead at the start, I think we can keep the on-track position, so let’s see what we can do.”

Andrea Stella, Team Principal

“Our performance in Qualifying reflects our current standing compared to our direct rivals: we’re around third or fourth place, with very tight gaps between us. Clearly, our grid positions could have been better had it not been for Lando’s time being deleted due to track limits and the difficulties we faced in completing our two runs in Q3.

“The conditions were very tricky: the wind and the changing track conditions made it difficult to replicate a corner from one lap to the next. Overall, though, I think the result is fair. We are aware that the MCL40 has good potential, but it is very difficult to extract, and this leaves the drivers with little or no margin for error, which – as we saw today – can prove costly.

“Now we need to focus on tomorrow’s race. Tyre degradation and the various possible strategies could create opportunities: for our part, we need to manage the race well, make up positions and put ourselves in a position to fight for the podium. It won’t be easy starting from the fourth row, but we’ll give it our all.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Lando Norris of Great Britain driving the (1) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Oscar Piastri of Australia driving the (81) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

Racing Bulls

Racing Bulls have been in and around the top 10 all weekend, so it was no real surprise to see both drivers make it to Q3. They left it late to do so, the last to cross the line at the end of Q2. Once into the top 10 shootout, the team opted to run Arvid Lindblad once while Liam Lawson went for an early shower. With the former taking a five-place grid drop, that tactic made sense and means Lindblad starts 14th tomorrow instead of 15th.

Liam Lawson, 10th, No time set in Q3

"It's been a strong weekend so far. Ahead of Qualifying, we decided that I wouldn't run again if we had both cars in Q3. We weren't fighting the front teams, so this strategy meant that I would save tyres for the race and help Arvid move up the grid given his penalty. We don't normally get to go through to Q3 with two sets of tyres left, so naturally I was keen to go again. That being said, we were fighting for P9 anyway, so it made sense for us as a team. We have a strong race car, so I'm looking forward to getting out there again tomorrow."

Arvid Lindblad, 9th, 1 :36.049

"It hasn’t been an easy weekend so far on our side. We started on the back foot, as I’ve been a few tenths off Liam in every session, but when it mattered most, we put everything together and made it through to Q3. I’m really pleased with the work we’ve done, so a big thank you to everyone involved. We kept chipping away and making small improvements in every run, and overall, I’m very happy with my lap. It’s a great track to drive and one that offers plenty of overtaking opportunities, with its heavy and wide braking zones. We’ll start a little further back tomorrow due to the engine penalty, but my focus is on maximising my performance behind the wheel and putting myself in the best possible position to make up some ground in the race."

Tim Goss, Chief Technical Officer

"It was a really successful Qualifying session for VCARB today in Austin, with both Liam and Arvid making Q3. We have brought some significant aerodynamic updates to the car for this event, and once again our pipeline of upgrades and correlation to track has proved it is delivering. The car has taken another step forwards in performance and both drivers have made the most of exploiting this.

“The day started reasonably smoothly in FP3, with a strong performance on the Medium tyre. We then tested some small adjustments to control settings for the final Soft tyre run, which was less than perfect. So we unwound these ahead of Qualifying knowing that the car setup and balance was fundamentally in a good place.

“Both drivers successfully made the cut-off in Q1, with Liam delivering such a good lap, we could afford to save a set of Soft tyres and sit out the second run. The main battleground for us was Q2 which was tight once again. However, both drivers were confident with the car and delivered clean laps to progress to Q3. From here we took a tactical decision not to compete. The bigger prize is the race on Sunday for which we decided we would benefit from saving a new Soft tyre set for each driver, rather than using them in Q3. We completed a steady lap with Arvid on used tyres, just to place him ahead of Liam and limit his grid penalty by one place.

“Race pace and tyre management will be important tomorrow, and we look forward to showing the VCARB 03 and the drivers have the pace to bring home some points."

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Tenth placed qualifier Liam Lawson of New Zealand and Visa Cash App Racing Bulls looks on during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Arvid Lindblad of Great Britain driving the (41) Visa Cash App Racing Bulls VCARB 03 RB Ford on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Mark Thompson/Getty Images)

Alpine

Alpine improved from Friday into Saturday, with Pierre Gasly suddenly looking like top 10 material in final practice. He had a nervous time of it in Qualifying after losing his first lap to track limits in Q1 to leave him as the only driver without a lap time. But he did just about scrape through and then came close to making Q3. But he will gain a place when Lindblad’s penalty is applied and thus starts in the top 10. As for Franco Colapinto, he qualified 14th but drops to the back after his own penalty is applied.

Pierre Gasly, 11th, 1:35.080

“I did not leave much on the table in Q2, so I am not too disappointed with the outcome as that is just where our performance has been this weekend. Of course, missing out by 0.022secs to Q3 is a tough one but I was pleased with my lap in the end and we move up to P10 on the grid due to the penalty for Arvid [Lindblad]. It's been tricky to nail a lap here and it has been a challenging weekend for us overall with the car. We are still in the mix for points tomorrow and that is the aim: to take the fight to Racing Bulls. I need to target them at the start, try to get ahead and then see what we can do from there. There's a lot of work to do tomorrow but I am glad we are in a position to capitalise and I'll be giving it my all to return to the points.”

Franco Colapinto, 14th, 1:35.722

“Going into Qualifying today, we knew we would be slightly up against it with the grid penalty but expected more in terms of where we eventually ended up on the timesheets. When you know a penalty is coming you still try and do your best and minimise the impact with a higher grid slot. The pace just lacked today, and the car is seemingly not as suited here as it is at other tracks, which we need to understand why that was the case. We have worked hard all weekend on race set-up and saved some tyres, so let's hope for a better Sunday, and take the fight to those ahead of us.”

Steve Nielsen, Managing Director

“It has not been an easy weekend so far and we line up for tomorrow's race with one car starting near the back due to a penalty and one car up and amongst it inside the points. It seems this track with the conditions and the bumps has proved difficult for everyone – not just us – and car balance for drivers has been tough to read lap by lap. Sometimes it does not click, sometimes it does, like we saw with Pierre in Q2 for example where his first lap was quite far off, a little puzzling for him and the team, and then his second was well managed and pretty close to the absolute maximum. In the end, he moves up to P10 and his focus is directly on Liam [Lawson] in the Racing Bulls ahead. For Franco, we know it will be a tough ask to climb through the field from the back. That being said, we know Franco tends to make fast starts and his aim will be to capitalise on our promising high fuel pace from Friday Practice and try to work his way towards the points-paying positions.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Pierre Gasly of France driving the (10) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: (EDITOR'S NOTE: Tonal effects have been applied to this image) Franco Colapinto of Argentina driving the (43) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Hector Vivas - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Audi

With Gabriel Bortoleto set to start at the back after taking a raft of new power unit components, the Brazilian adding even more to his pool on Saturday, Audi opted to try and utilise the tow at the Circuit of The Americas. It nearly worked too, but Nico Hulkenberg picked up some traffic before getting into the slipstream behind his team mate and thus could not quite do enough to progress. But he gains a place thanks to Lindblad dropping back, and is certainly in the mix for points if he can start well tomorrow.

Nico Hulkenberg, 12th, 1:35.158

"It was another very tight Qualifying session, and unfortunately we just missed out on Q3 by a tenth. My first run in Q2 was pretty good, but we couldn't quite find that extra bit of lap time in the second run. In this midfield, those small margins make all the difference.

"Still, starting from P11 tomorrow, we're in a decent position. It's going to be a long, physical race, especially with how bumpy this track is. The start and opening lap will be important, but I think we can race the cars around us and have a good fight. There's plenty to play for, so let's see what we can make of it."

Gabriel Bortoleto, 13th, 1:35.691

“The car felt really good in Q1, and that helped me putting together a really satisfying lap, apart from the last corner. I knew I needed to give it everything out there, as I would be helping Nico with the tow in Q2, so it was nice to get that lap in. We know we have to start from the back tomorrow, so there was no real reason to push for more in Qualifying.

"Still, I am optimistic for the race. Obviously, it is not easy when you are starting from the back, but overtaking is possible here, and I believe there will be opportunities for us. We need to be ready to take advantage of them whenever they come.”

Allan McNish, Racing Director

“Today’s Qualifying session was obviously not standard. Knowing Gabi would be starting from the back due to his grid penalty, we adjusted our approach to give Nico the best possible opportunity. Gabi played an important role in that and executed the tows very well. Ultimately, we fell just a tenth short of Q3, which shows how fine the margins are in this midfield. Nico qualified P12 and will line up P11 following Lindblad’s penalty, leaving us in a good position to challenge for points with the race pace we’ve shown. Gabi faces a more demanding afternoon, but his determination and ability to respond in difficult circumstances makes me sure that he will work his way forward.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Nico Hulkenberg of Germany driving the (27) Audi F1 Team R26 on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Gabriel Bortoleto of Brazil driving the (5) Audi F1 Team R26 on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

Aston Martin

Fernando Alonso progressed to Q2 for Aston Martin for the second time in the last three races, in what was good news for the team. Even better news is that when all the grid penalties are applied, he will actually start up in 12th and right in the thick of the action. Lance Stroll did not escape Q1 and cut a frustrated figure afterwards, complaining over the radio about a raft of issues with his car.

Fernando Alonso, 15th, 1:35.818

“The performance of the car seems slightly better for us here in Austin so far and it's our third Q2 of the season. We will start a little higher thanks to some penalties around us, but that does put us out of our natural position. I think we could be defending more than attacking, but anything can happen here and it should be an interesting race.”

Lance Stroll, 18th, 1:36.677

“I felt pretty good in the car yesterday, but we lost a lot of running today in FP3 because of kerb damage, which limited our progress. In Qualifying I had a lot of oversteer and no rear grip. It was the most challenging session of the weekend so far. We’ll look for opportunities tomorrow.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Fernando Alonso of Spain driving the (14) Aston Martin F1 Team AMR26 Honda on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Mark Thompson/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Lance Stroll of Canada driving the (18) Aston Martin F1 Team AMR26 Honda on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

Haas

Not to be for Haas, who looked strong heading into Qualifying after another solid practice session for Ollie Bearman. Esteban Ocon has not been able to extract the same pace from his VF-26 as his team mate and exited at the first time of asking, but Bearman made it to Q2. He initially qualified 13th but his last flying run was deleted for track limits and thus he dropped down the order.

Oliver Bearman, 16th, 1:36.031

“I felt like I did a good job to get out of Q1, as the car wasn’t feeling quite how I wanted it. In Q2, things came together a bit better, and my final lap was very good, but sadly, it got deleted for track limits. I thought I was on the edge at Turn 11, looks like I was just over. It’s so hard though, as with the camera view that I saw, with the glare of the sun and everything, it seems like you’re playing with millimetres here, and you can’t tell here when you’re close to the line. I have to go for it, especially in Q2, but it’s a shame as I haven’t had track limits all weekend. I’m a bit disappointed in myself, but I know we’ll go again tomorrow.”

Esteban Ocon, 17th, 1:36.531

“I think there are some positives in the fact that we did improve a little bit. The fundamental car characteristics remain the same, unfortunately, and we’re still fighting with inconsistency. We usually see that when we’re fighting these issues, it’s not enough to get out of Q1. It’s been a while since that happened, so it’s a shame that it’s happened here. It was a good lap, it was as fast as the car could go, but tomorrow we need to be opportunistic.”

Ayao Komatsu, Team Principal

“I think today’s Qualifying result is pretty disappointing, especially on Ollie’s side, as we were building up quite well throughout the weekend. His track limits violation was marginal, but we accept it, and I think we nearly got the most out of it on Ollie’s side of the garage. On Esteban’s side, I think we got there in the end in terms of car set-up, but if we don’t build up from a good baseline in FP1, then it’s very hard to catch up. Our starting positions are challenging, but tomorrow – going into Turn 1, anything can happen. So, we need to focus on getting the balance of the car right and having clean operations, both on strategy and pit-stops, and see what we can do.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Oliver Bearman of Great Britain driving the (87) Haas F1 VF-26 Ferrari on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Esteban Ocon of France driving the (31) Haas F1 VF-26 Ferrari on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Peter Fox/Getty Images)

Williams

Williams have struggled in Austin from word go, and they did not find any answers in terms of set-up for Qualifying. Both drivers were still sliding wide, with Alex Albon especially frustrated after coming out early for his final run in Q1 before the track had fully evolved. But such were Albon's and Carlos Sainz' struggles, it likely made no difference with both drivers exiting at the first time of asking.

Carlos Sainz, 19th, 1:36.770

“It’s been a tough weekend and probably more difficult than we expected, however ahead of Qualifying, we made some setup changes that actually made the car feel better. My last lap was coming together very well, with very strong first and second sectors, but I made a mistake into turn 15 which potentially cost us some positions. In any case, tomorrow’s race will be tough for us as I don’t expect our pace to be enough to fight our way up the order. However, there are more things to learn from the car and I’m looking forward to executing our best race possible and see where that takes us."

Alex Albon, 20th, 1:36.967

“Not the cleanest Saturday. We went out quite early at the end of Q1, so we'll look at the run plan and review the data from today. I'm still searching for rhythm with this car and the tyres. We're throwing everything at it, and trying to maximise the pace that we do have, but we also knew this track would expose our weaknesses. We might try something different tomorrow and see what comes our way."

James Vowles, Team Principal

“This weekend’s been tough since the first laps of FP1. We haven’t had the pace. I think there was more in it today, we didn’t get it all right, but the reality is it’s a few positions and the disappointment is the gap to the top 10 is large. But that news isn’t new to us – we know the challenge in front of us and what we have to accomplish for next year. That doesn’t make it easier on any given weekend but we’ll give our all tomorrow and carry on maximising our learnings for next year's car."

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Alexander Albon of Thailand driving the (23) Williams FW48 Mercedes on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Carlos Sainz of Spain driving the (55) Williams FW48 Mercedes on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

Cadillac

Not to be for Cadillac at their home race, with neither car able to progress out of Q1. Sergio Perez took the intra-team honours for the second race in a row, just pipping Valtteri Bottas by less than a tenth. They don’t start on the back row tomorrow, that honour goes to Colapinto and Bortoleto. But it looks set to be a long afternoon for the home team, who remain without enough pace to fight too much further forward.

Sergio Perez, 21st, 1:37.433

“Unfortunately, I didn’t get the maximum out of the car. I think we were about half a second ahead, but I had an issue with the K (Kinetic Energy Recovery System) and basically got on the throttle a little bit too early because I had traffic in the final corner, and the system just got confused. It’s a little difficult to understand exactly what happened, but I lost two tenths in the final sector that I definitely could have gained. That would have put us a little bit closer to Williams, but it wasn’t enough.

“Tomorrow is going to be tougher. This track is very hard on the right tyres, and it's going to be a challenge to preserve them. So, yeah, it’s going to be an interesting one tomorrow. I’m not expecting anything great, but we’ll give it our best.”

Valtteri Bottas, 22nd, 1:37.523

“I was hoping that we could be closer to Williams, but they have been out of our reach, particularly on one lap pace. It's been an interesting weekend so far as we've been exploring different set-up options because of how bumpy the circuit is. We've explored several directions and in the end, I think we’ve found a good place for the car so that Checo and I can extract the most out of the package we have. We know on paper that the race is going to be a challenge for us, but we’re always ready for any opportunities that come our way and if they do, we’ll be sure to put ourselves into the mix.”

Marcin Budkowski, Team Principal

“As a team we have been looking forward to today’s qualifying at our second home race of the season in Austin. It’s been energising to see so many of our fans during the build up to qualifying today.

“The team executed our plan for Qualifying well but it has exposed our current weaknesses in performance and package. Regardless, both Checo and Valtteri drove well to extract the most from the MAC-26. Some of our competitors have grid penalties for tomorrow and our focus will be on looking at the options available to move forward in the race. It will be hot, bumpy and hard for the tyres, so our aim is to get both cars to the finish in front of a home crowd.”

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Twenty-first placed qualifier Sergio Perez of Mexico and Cadillac F1 Team walks in the Pitlane during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Valtteri Bottas of Finland driving the (77) Cadillac F1 Team MAC-26 Ferrari on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of United States at Circuit of The Americas on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Mark Thompson/Getty Images)

Pirelli

Dario Marrafuschi, Pirelli Motorsport Director

“The Free Practice session today provided indications consistent with those that emerged yesterday. The C4 confirmed a performance advantage over the C3 in terms of both grip and lap time, a factor that ensures clear differentiation between the available options. In race pace running, however, the two softer compounds proved to be very closely matched, increasing the number of strategic scenarios available to the teams.

"The simulations indicate that a one-stop strategy remains the most effective solution in terms of overall race time. The Soft-Medium combination could be chosen by more than one team in order to maximise the grip advantage offered by the red-banded tyre.

"The Hard nevertheless remains a valid option for the second stint, regardless of whether the race is started on the Soft or the Medium. An early neutralisation could in fact encourage teams to complete the remainder of the Grand Prix on the C2.

"Should degradation prove higher than expected, a two-stop strategy based on a Soft-Medium-Soft sequence could also become an attractive option. The time difference compared with the one-stop strategy remains relatively small, but track position and the potential impact of traffic must also be taken into account. Ultimately, it will be the evolution of track conditions and tomorrow’s temperatures that determine the choices made by the teams.”

title: Max Verstappen fires back at Austin boss after 'unacceptable' comment response
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has claimed that Circuit of the Americas boss Bobby Epstein "would not be able to walk" if he experienced the bumps at Austin.

Verstappen has been outspoken across the United States Grand Prix weekend at the state of the track surface, including severe bumps at Turns 1, 4, 5, and 19.

The one at Turn 1 is in the braking zone if a driver is attempting to make an overtake, with Verstappen explaining that he suffered a 9G spine compression in 2025, so bad were the bumps.

Lando Norris has spoken of the need to take headache tablets to combat the effects of the bumps, as COTA boss Epstein explained that he felt the track surface was fine, except for Turn 1, which he claimed the circuit was unaware of.

Addressing Epstein's response, Verstappen offered him an invitation to sample the track in F1 machinery to experience the bumps for himself.

"I invite him to drive my car," Verstappen told media, including RacingNews365, when presented with Epstein's comments.

"I’ll see him get out again within five laps; he won’t even be able to walk.

"In that really fast sector, between Turns 4 and 5, there are huge bumps.

"I get that the surface here is a problem, but you should have taken a closer look at that beforehand."

[Article continues below].

Verstappen also makes F1 and FIA point

Verstappen also believes that F1 and the FIA share some of the blame for the nature of the track surface.

"They do understand what we’re saying, but you have to figure out how to solve this for the future," he said.

"You could just lay down new asphalt, but a year or two later you’ll have the same problem again. You really need to dig deeper into the issue.

"Ultimately, I think the FIA and F1 need to be stricter about this.

"I get that it all costs a lot of money, but if you know the subsoil is shifting, you just have to dig it all up and lay a new foundation underneath."

title: Lewis Hamilton makes 'hard to compete' claim in Red Bull Austin prediction
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton believes Red Bull's superior power unit will make it "hard to compete" in the United States GP, such is Ferrari's deficit.

Hamilton will start fifth in Austin, and at the tail of the Red Bull-Ferrari group, with Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar both ahead of Charles Leclerc and Hamilton, with Kimi Antonelli on pole.

A major issue with the SF-26 all season has been its lack of top-end straight line speed, brought about by Ferrari's initial decision to opt for a small turbo, which, whilst providing excellent slow-speed drivability, lacks pure grunt.

In contrast, Red Bull's first in-house power unit has been adjudged by the FIA's ADUO process as the best ICE on the grid, with the unit particularly strong in a straight line.

With both Ferraris set to start behind both Red Bulls, Hamilton, whilst expressing how difficult it was to overtake at the Circuit of the Americas, predicted it would be "hard to compete" with the power of the Red Bulls.

"We're fourth and fifth, and it is very hard to overtake here," Hamilton told media, including RacingNews365.

"If you are P2 on the grid, it's hard to beat someone since 2012, and it took a lot to get past [Sebastian] Vettel back then, but maybe with strategy we can progress.

"We can get a good run up to Turn 1, and there are opportunities with the strategy, so we shall see."

Turning to the Red Bull advantage on the straights, Hamilton added that he felt it was "hard to compete with" the RBPT-Ford power unit.

"I mean it varies, and I haven't seen the actual numbers this weekend, but [on Saturday morning], I think it was like three-tenths [advantage on the straights]," he said.

"In some places, it is three-to-five tenths but maybe four tenths, and it is pretty impressive.

"On the overlays, our engine starts clipping into Turn 1, and theirs just keeps going, so that's hard to compete with.

"If we had the same power as them, we'd be right there in the battle, and we know that's the case so we will try to make the best we can now."

title: Oscar Piastri offers 'motocross' warning over major Austin F1 bump
excerpt:
The bumps at the Circuit of the Americas are causing major talking points for drivers - with Oscar Piastri offering his take.

Oscar Piastri believes the bump in the Turn 1 braking zone at the Circuit of the Americas is akin to a "motocross jump".

Throughout the weekend at the United States GP, drivers have been critical of the track surface, including Max Verstappen calling the bumps "unacceptable."

The Austin track is built on former marshland near to Austin Bergstrom International Airport, with the underlying ground shifting as a result.

COTA boss Bobby Epstein feels the track surface is acceptable, aside from into Turn 1, where McLaren's Piastri believes the bump is akin to a "motocross jump", especially under braking.

"I think the majority of the track is probably better than what it has been in previous years," Piastri told media, including RacingNews365, about the bumps.

"But the bump into Turn 1 is a bit like a motocross jump, and then the one into Turn 19 is not that much better.

"So in qualifying, it is not too bad as you brake after the bump, but in the race, you're braking right on that bump, especially if you are overtaking someone into Turn 1.

"We've spoken with the FIA about it, and I'm sure it will be fixed for next year."

[Article continues below].

Piastri's qualifying reflections

As for his qualifying, Piastri will start seventh at Austin, having been promoted up one place after team-mate Lando Norris had a time deleted for track limits.

However, the McLaren was just over eight-tenths slower than the pole time of Kimi Antonelli as both Piastri and Norris continue to struggle to extract performance from the tricky MCL40.

"It has been tough from lap one; just trying to get performance out of the car has been very, very challenging," Piastri noted.

"At points in qualifying for Lando, at least it looked like there was potential in it, and I think we both felt there was potential in it, but the difference between extracting that potential or not is like half a second, so it's been very, very tough to get that lap time out of the car.

"I've not managed it at all. But I think when either of us has really pushed the boundaries, we can't keep it on the track. So it's been very challenging for sure.

"I think we're probably a couple of tenths off Mercedes and Red Bull, and naturally as drivers, you try and make that up as well.

"So I think there's probably a little element of that, but I think the car in general just needs to be driven on a knife edge all the time, and I think at a track like this, where there are so many sequences of corners, so many bumps, it really doesn't take much at all for it to go very wrong.

"I did a reasonable job in the areas that I really wanted to focus on, but just trying to put a lap together has been almost impossible."

title: Fred Vasseur rejects 'bulls**t' excuse for sudden Ferrari qualifying flop
excerpt:
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has rejected the idea of the wind affecting his drivers in United States Grand Prix qualifying as "bulls**t."

Throughout practice in Austin, Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton topped every session, with Hamilton topping an FP3 session for the first time in over two years, since the 2024 Italian GP.

This made the Scuderia favourite for pole position in Texas, but both drivers did not carry over their practice pace into qualifying, with Leclerc taking fourth on the grid and Hamilton fifth, with 0.044s between them in the Monegasque's favour.

Leclerc was 0.232s slower than pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli, who had left the door open for others to overtake him after a mistake on his second run in Q3.

Nobody could capitalise, leaving both Ferraris also behind Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, as Vasseur demanded a better execution of qualifying to extract the result he felt was in the SF-26.

"There are mixed feelings for sure because I think the potential was there all over the weekend and we had good pace in all the free practice, and until the last corner, we are fighting for pole," Vasseur told Sky Sports F1.

"It is as it is, and it is all part of the game, but I think [the race] will be a different exercise, and it will be difficult with a lot of degradation, but for sure, there is a bit of frustration because we had very good potential until the last corner of Q3.

"We were in better shape. Q2 was a bit faster for everybody [than Q1], and we all struggled to improve in Q3; perhaps it was a bit of wind, but it is also a distraction for the drivers, but okay, it is the same for everybody.

"We can't complain about the wind; this would be bulls**t, and we have to do a better job on the last lap, because we had the potential to be at least on the front row."

[Article continues below].

'From hero to zero'

Vasseur also explained how a minor misjudgment was capable of turning a driver from a 'hero to zero' in the difficult conditions.

"For a couple of hundredths, you can move from P2 to P6 or P7, from hero to zero, and it's a gust of wind or one metre [earlier or later] on the breaking point," Vasseur continued.

"We have to stay calm when we are speaking about potential. It's a different story, but it's F1, and it's like this from now for a couple of races."

title: How Kimi Antonelli can win the 2026 F1 drivers' world championship today
excerpt:
When can Kimi Antonelli win the 2026 F1 drivers' championship title?

Following the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix, Kimi Antonelli holds a 102-point lead over Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

No other driver is within 100 points of the Italian, who is increasingly set to become the youngest F1 world champion and shatter Sebastian Vettel's record of 23 years, 4 months, 11 days by over three years.

Antonelli, who turned 20 in August 2026, has dominated the season, and has his first championship point in the United States Grand Prix at Austin.

The article continues below.

THIS ARTICLE WILL BE UPDATED FOLLOWING EVERY GRAND PRIX UNTIL ANTONELLI WINS THE 2026 F1 WORLD DRIVERS' TITLE.

How Kimi Antonelli can win the title today

After the Singapore Grand Prix, there are six races scheduled to take place in the season, each worth 25 points.

This gives a total of 150 points remaining in the championship, with Antonelli holding that 102-point lead after third in Singapore whilst Russell picked up two points for ninth. Antonelli also holds a 111-point lead over Lewis Hamilton.

Antonelli will start on pole position in Austin, with Hamilton fifth and Russell sixth.

For Antonelli to win the title in the United States, the following events must happen.

Antonelli wins the United States Grand Prix

Russell finishes ninth or lower

Hamilton finishes fifth or lower

This is the only combination of results that will see Antonelli crowned in Austin. If Antonelli were to win, Russell was ninth, but Hamilton was fourth, the title race would go on to Mexico City next week.

Should Antonelli win, he will move to 127 points clear of Russell after his ninth grand prix win of the season, with 125 points left on the table.

He would also move 136 points clear of Hamilton.

Russell would be required to score at least four points for an eighth-place finish or better to reduce the gap under 125.

Hamilton would be required to finish at least fourth to bring his deficit back down to 124 points, with a fifth-place finish and an Antonelli win meaning his deficit would be 126 with 125 left.

If Antonelli does win the race and Russell is ninth, the points gap would be 125 points exactly.

But by dint of having nine grand prix wins to Russell's three, Antonelli would win as Russell could not eclipse his tally of wins in the remaining five races.

Should Russell then go onto win in Mexico City, Sao Paulo, Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi, he would draw level on points if Antonelli did not score again - but as points ties are broken firstly by number of wins, Antonelli's 9 to Russell's potential 8 would be game, set, match, and championship for the Italian.

Should Antonelli win the title in the United States, he will be 20 years, 2 months, 0 days old.

title: Kimi Antonelli addresses 'different' feeling as first F1 title point arrives
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has admitted this weekend "does feel a little bit different" after claiming pole position for the United States Grand Prix, a result that hands the Mercedes driver his first opportunity to be crowned world champion in Austin.

The Italian topped qualifying at the Circuit of the Americas with a lap of 1:34.035, edging out Max Verstappen by 0.179 seconds and Isack Hadjar by 0.215 seconds in a tight top three.

Charles Leclerc, Lewis Hamilton and George Russell rounded out the top six, with Hamilton and Russell being the only drivers who can deny Antonelli the title.

For the 20-year-old to become world champion in Austin, Antonelli needs to win the race while Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Russell finishes outside the top nine.

Anything less from either rival, or a slip from Antonelli himself, pushes the title fight into the remaining rounds in Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Speaking to select media, including RacingNews365, after securing pole, Antonelli made clear his focus remained on the race itself rather than the numbers around it.

"I'm just going to try to do the best race I can," Antonelli said. "I'm going to try to win, and then we'll see what happens. But, you know, it's good to finish qualifying like this.

"Of course, Sunday is going to be a new day. Max has been very quick, Isack also has been very quick, so just need to get a good start, and then we'll see from there what we can do."

Kimi Antonelli embracing title pursuit opportunity

By claiming pole and with both Hamilton and Russell a few positions behind, Antonelli faces a better chance than expected of securing the title in the United States and becoming F1's youngest champion.

Asked whether the prospect of wrapping up the title changed how the weekend felt, Antonelli acknowledged a shift in his approach without losing sight of the job at hand.

"I mean, it does feel a little bit different, but the goal stays the same," added Antonelli. "I just need to keep doing my job, and actually, I feel like I can enjoy the driving and everything more.

"But of course, we still have to do the race, still have to try and win, and then, of course, we'll see what happens. But yeah, I feel like I can enjoy it a bit more because obviously I'm in a very good position. But still, the mindset is always the same."

title: Lando Norris makes astonishing claim over Austin F1 qualifying struggles
excerpt:
Lando Norris has claimed his McLaren was the "hardest car I've ever had to drive" as he struggled through qualifying at the United States Grand Prix.

McLaren has looked unconvincing throughout the weekend in Austin, with its front-running rivals running more consistently at the head of the timesheets.

Its struggles were amplified during qualifying, with Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris slumping to seventh and eighth, respectively.

Norris was originally positioned in sixth place before his final lap time was deleted for track limits.

While the lost two positions were disappointing, Norris asserted his struggles were deeper than what the lap time suggested.

"The car was very strong in terms of pace, just insanely difficult to drive," Norris told media including RacingNews365.

"[It was] probably the hardest car I've ever had to drive in my life, but it was good enough for P2.

"I should be P2, but I'm P8, so clearly I did a very bad job today."

[Article continues below]

Norris highlights biggest McLaren weakness

Norris pinpointed the final sector as McLaren's biggest weak point, stating the team is "dreadful" through that part of the circuit.

"The car was good enough for P2, the car was quick. It's just nasty to drive.

"A good result is possible. I have faith that we can get a good result tomorrow. I don't know how easy it's going to be to overtake and things like that.

"For a lot of the track, we seem on par. We struggle a lot in sector three, in the very slow speed, we're pretty dreadful. But tomorrow is a new day."

title: Jeremy Clarkson branded 'unacceptable' after Franco Colapinto remark
excerpt:
Franco Colapinto's management team have branded a comment made by Jeremy Clarkson as "unacceptable" at the United States Grand Prix.

Former Top Gear host Clarkson is a guest of the team at this weekend's Austin race, and prior to qualifying, was interviewed on Sky Sports F1, where he discussed Colapinto's 10-place grid penalty for power unit component changes.

The Clarkson's Farm presenter said: "Franco's got a grid penalty for being Argentine. Probably, well, I'd give him one for that.

"That's just because of what happened when we went there."

Clarkson's dislike of Argentina stems from a 2014 episode of Top Gear filmed in Patagonia when he drove a car with a number plate alleged to be a reference to the 1982 Falklands War between Argentina, who claim the territory and the United Kingdom, who holds it.

He, co-presenters Richard Hammond and James May and the rest of the crew were forced to abandon the shoot and flee to the Chilean border whilst being attacked by locals. The number plate 'H982 FKL' was later proved to be the genuine one issued when the car was built, and the crew had not noticed the perceived reference to the war.

Taking to social media, Colapinto's management team issued a statement, calling out Clarkson's comments - a week after Colapinto issued a statement of his own calling on his loyal fan-base to stop abusing other drivers on social media.

"Jeremy Clarkson’s comments about Franco’s nationality were completely unacceptable," wrote Jamie Campbell-Walter.

"There is no place for remarks like this in Formula 1, regardless of who makes them or whether they are intended as a joke.

We have worked hard to promote respect and put an end to hostility and abuse.

"That respect must go both ways. We cannot ask anyone to behave responsibly while accepting comments like these from prominent figures visiting our sport.

"Franco and his supporters deserve better than this. Let’s not allow this to undo the progress we’ve made and rise above malicious comments."

The Alpine team also issued a statement, without naming Clarkson.

"We're aware of the comments made in a recent TV ​interview from a guest of the team in Austin," said the statement, as quoted by Reuters.

"We would like ​to reiterate that these are personal views and do not align with the team's values of promoting kindness and ‌respect. ⁠Franco is our driver and has our full support."

After his 10-place grid penalty, Colapinto is due to start the Austin race in 21st, with team-mate Pierre Gasly in 10th.

The race is due to get underway at 15:00 local time, 20:00 GMT.

title: Max Verstappen issues 'eff off' response after hate towards 'great' team-mate
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has hit out at online trolls after team-mate Chris Lulham was subjected to abuse following a costly mistake at last weekend's GT World Challenge Europe finale in Portimao.

Lulham, who races for the GT squad Verstappen founded, was handed a drive-through penalty after contact with Luca Stolz's Winward Mercedes during an inside overtake attempt.

The incident dropped the Team Verstappen Racing entry from podium contention to 24th place, and triggered a wave of personal attacks on Lulham across social media.

Verstappen, who hand-picked Lulham to make the step up from sim racing with Team Redline into real-world GT competition, addressed the abuse, initially via an online statement after the race, and again during his media duties ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix in Austin.

Asked whether more needed to be done about online abuse, or whether he felt nothing was being done, Verstappen did not hold back.

"No," he said, speaking to the media, including RacingNews365. "But that starts with the social media companies themselves, where you can make many troll accounts as well, with no real names or [IP] addresses attached, and people can say whatever they like online.

"For me personally, I don't care. If it targets me, they can all eff off.

"But when it's to one of my drivers who is young, and not used to this kind of pressure and attention, and when they start writing these kinds of things, it's quite extreme. That's why I felt the need to put that statement out.

"Of course, I've talked to him about it, and I've tried to make sure that he doesn't read about it too much."

[Article continues below]

Verstappen - 'We all make mistakes'

The four-time champion went on to stress that he has no issue with the error itself, framing it as part of a learning curve for his young protégé.

"I know his character," said Verstappen. "He's quite relaxed, but it's still not nice and definitely not deserved because, first of all, he's just a great guy.

"Of course, he's learning. We're all learning. We all make mistakes. That's not a problem for me.

"He did such a great job all weekend, and then [he made] a tiny little misjudgment. Of course, it gave us a penalty, but there is no need to throw any hate towards him.

"That's why it was very important to make that statement."

title: Lewis Hamilton opposes Max Verstappen after vocal F1 critcism
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has stated he enjoys the bumps around the Circuit of the Americas, highlighting that they add "character" to the track.

The host track of the United States Grand Prix has long been known to be a challenge for the drivers due to its bumpy surface.

This weekend, Verstappen has been particularly vocal about the strain that the bumps have placed on him.

The four-time champion revealed that he had scans done on his back, which revealed damage to his spinal discs from the bumpy surface.

But Hamilton has stated that he is a fan of the uncertainty they pose for the driver trying to put together a strong lap.

"I personally like the bumps, it adds character to the track," Hamilton told media including RacingNews365.

"I love the challenge of that because you know the car is moving and you have to correct it.

"In a perfect world, it would be a flat track, but then there would be a lack of character. That's what gives this track that little bit more.

"It's already a great layout. The bumps give it a bit more.

"Turn 1 is not a problem for us at all. Turn 19 and Turn 9 are a little bit bumpy, but everyone is in the same boat.

"People are complaining, but I'm 42 and my back is fine."

[Article continues below]

Hamilton perplexed by qualifying struggle

Hamilton entered the qualifying session at COTA on Saturday hoping to fight for pole position after setting the fastest lap time in FP3 earlier in the day.

However, Ferrari's form slipped away as qualifying progressed, with Hamilton only able to muster sixth on the grid.

The seven-time champion admitted he was at a loss to explain what went wrong.

"I haven't looked at the data," Hamilton said.

"Through the weekend, we looked at the straight. Up to Turn 1, when we cut power, they [Red Bull] just keep pulling.

"That's similar in other places, like going into Turn 11. I think it might be similar into 12, but then the rest of the lap, you see it on the overlay.

"But I don't know what happened. My car felt pretty good. The lap was solid. They were just quicker."

title: Red Bull young star seals emotional title after stunning drive
excerpt:
Alisha Palmowski has been crowned 2026 F1 Academy champion after clinching the title at the Circuit of the Americas, wrapping up the all-female championship with the season finale in Las Vegas still to come.

The Campos Racing driver, racing under the Red Bull Academy Programme, sealed the crown in Saturday's reverse grid race, charging from eighth on the grid to finish second behind Ferrari's Alba Larsen.

Palmowski had already laid the foundations for the title earlier in the Austin weekend by winning Friday's opening race, building an advantage that proved unassailable before Sunday's feature race had even been run.

Emma Felbermayr, Larsen and Nina Gademan had kept the fight alive for much of the campaign, but none could close the gap in Texas to Palmowski.

As champion, Palmowski is set to receive F1 Academy's funded progression package, which typically includes a seat and testing allocation in a higher single-seater category such as FRECA or GB3.

The exact points margin over her rivals will only be confirmed once the feature race in Austin and the season-closing round in Las Vegas have been completed.

Her Formula 1 future remains a longer-term prospect, with her affiliation to the Red Bull Academy Programme likely to shape whatever comes next in her junior single-seater career.
